title: Discourse topic moves can bypass destination-category visibility checks
product: Discourse topic and message category-move authorization
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not identified for this finding)
summary: The project’s security fix makes topic moves into a destination category require that the user can see that category. The change applies to moderators and members, and also to converting a message to a public topic or changing a queued topic category; existing admin and moderator exceptions for visible categories are preserved. The source does not detail a particular data exposure or attacker scenario, so impact is limited here to the authorization boundary bypass described by the maintainers.
ai_role: The official Discourse release changelog identifies the main security change (#45852, backported as #45854) as discovered by Anthropic OSS Scanner under ANT-2026-ADPDEAPP. Anthropic’s scanner documentation says its fast-track reports are generated directly by its strongest models; the specific model/version is not identified.
classification_note: The project classifies the change as a security fix and explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner. No CVE/GHSA is named in the reviewed primary sources; the original pull request #45852 is the public issue identifier. No exploitation claim is made.
remediation_note: Category changes now require the user to see the destination category across direct topic moves, message-to-topic conversion, and queued-topic edits, while preserving documented admin/moderator permissions for categories they can see. The change was backported to releases 2026.10 (#45854), 2026.9 (#45855), and 2026.7 (#45856). Deployed patch status is not checked.
